observations.text: CRITICAL: Batch all DB operations. Never call harness-db.py one entry at a time. Each Bash call has hook overhead (~50ms). Write a Python script, one connection, all inserts. 12 entries = 1 call not 12
CRITICAL: Batch communication too. If you have 12 things to say to the commander, say them in 1 message not 12. Context window is precious. Every message costs. Consolidate
Don't overcorrect. When corrected, fix the specific thing. Don't swing to the opposite extreme. The correction is a data point, not a reversal of everything
setup-user-hooks.sh had 4 bugs: undefined vars, no removal logic, no cleanup, stale header. Fixed commit 924b380
Delegates have FULL capabilities: read, write, Bash, python3, SQLite, chrome-devtools, Vercel deploy, sub-delegation
Provenance 6-pillar definition SHIPPED in commit 40951fc: harness.md (6th component), CLAUDE.md (mission statement + design principle), framework-provenance.md (new framework doc, 232 lines)
Staleness blast radius: 3 fully stale, 5 partially stale files. All in scratch/harvesting. No committed code contaminated
Local dashboard on port 8411 is zombie process serving stale JSON. generate-dashboard.py has no --db flag

Session pointer trap: .scratch/.current-session points to the LATEST session, not necessarily YOUR session. When delegates run harness-db.py without --session, writes go to the wrong DB. Always use --session flag when the delegate's session differs from .current-session

# Proposal 3: reference/framework-provenance.md

**Status**: Ready for commander review
**Feedback incorporated**: /aitool-provenance naming (#3), audience=all aitools users (#3), aitools vs harness clarity (#5)

## Summary

New framework document for the Provenance component. Follows the
established framework-*.md pattern: discipline source, adoption
rationale, architectural decisions, maintenance.

## Proposed Content

```markdown
# Provenance

**Intent**: **Purpose**: Document the discipline behind provenance
tracking in the harness -- why every knowledge item tracks its basis,
how invalidation propagates, and how provenance connects to the
broader self-evolution loop. **Scope**: Discipline source, adoption
rationale, architectural decisions, and maintenance guidance. NOT the
provenance data itself (`/aitool-provenance` user-level skill for
read-only lookups, `/provenance` project-level skill in the aitools
repo for full CRUD). NOT the schema details
(`reference/harness-db-schema.sql`). NOT the governance principle
(future `.claude/rules/provenance.md`). **Audience**: All aitools
users. Agents producing or consuming knowledge items. Harness
architects extending the provenance system.

## Source Discipline

Six disciplines converge. Each solves a different facet of the problem
"what is this based on, and is the basis still valid?"

- **Truth maintenance** (de Kleer, ATMS, 1986) -- an inference engine
  that maintains dependency records between assumptions and derived
  conclusions. When an assumption is retracted, all dependent
  conclusions are marked OUT and the invalidation propagates through
  the full chain. Key concept: **nogood sets** -- when a combination
  of assumptions leads to a contradiction, recording that combination
  prevents future rediscovery of the same dead end.

- **Derivation chains** (W3C PROV, 2013) -- a standard for
  representing provenance: Entities (things), Activities (processes),
  Agents (responsible parties). Key relationships: `wa

observations.text: TERMINOLOGY RESOLUTION -- aitools vs harness: aitools is the CLI command and its source repo (one of six harness components: Orchestration). The harness is aitools plus everything it manages: tools, context, state, artifacts, frameworks, provenance. aitools is an INGREDIENT, the harness is the CAKE. The confusion exists because working IN the aitools repo makes them feel identical. Outside the repo, the distinction is clear. Resolution: two glossary entries, consistent usage going forward, no massive reconciliation needed.

SELF-AWARENESS PATTERNS from nobul-ops: Agent Operating Principles section adapted for aitools CLAUDE.md. Core patterns: (1) treat static files as assumptions -- context overrides files, (2) recency weight -- newest instruction wins, (3) verify don't infer -- read the file, don't guess, (4) carry forward operational learning -- burn tokens on quality not savings, (5) delegation duty -- subagents are blank slates, include everything. These are universal agent principles, not nobul-ops-specific. The provenance principle connects 'files may be stale' to 'provenance tracks staleness'.

Commit 40951fc: CLAUDE.md mission statement updated -- added 'Provenance-aware knowledge system' framing. New design principle added: 'Provenance-aware knowledge' covering dependency tracking, invalidation propagation, nogood sets, and staleness surfacing. Links to reference/framework-provenance.md.

observations.text: When launching a fix mission, give broad authority to DISCOVER and fix — not a constrained list of known issues. You do not know everything that is broken. The known issues are starting points, not the scope.

Do not launch bandit missions — uncoordinated one-off missions that overlap with running commanders. When a hurdle blocks a mission, fix it within the scope or delegate it properly. Never paper over it with a separate uncoordinated mission.
Nothing is ever fully working. Everything is continuously improving. The question is not "is it done" but "is it good enough to use now, and what improves next."
Do not show diffs or proposals in conversation. Show them on mission control where the commander can review with their own eyes and submit feedback. Conversation context is expensive.
When the commander says "both are orders, one depends on the other" — that means do A then B, not "A is approved." Do not interpret process instructions as approval gates.

Delegate capability test results: delegates have FULL access (read, write, Bash, python3, SQLite, chrome-devtools, Vercel deploy, sub-delegation). Earlier assumption of limited permissions was a permission-timing issue, not a fundamental limitation. But some delegates still hit Bash permission blocks — this is inconsistent and session-dependent.
